question: A pond has two populations, zooplankton and algae, and the trends in their population densities over time are shown in the figure. If a large number of a certain kind of fish (C) that specializes in eating zooplankton are released into the pond, after a period of time, only one population remains among the three populations A, B, and C in the pond. What relationships exist between C and B?
model_answer: Predation and competition (捕食和竞争)
cot_raw: The image shows two oscillating population curves over time on a graph with population density on the y-axis and time on the x-axis. Curve A (labeled A) is solid and peaks first, followed by curve B (labeled B) which is dashed and peaks slightly later, indicating a predator-prey relationship where A is the prey (algae) and B is the predator (zooplankton), with B following A in a classic Lotka-Volterra oscillation pattern. Based on this, A = algae, B = zooplankton, and C = fish that eats zooplankton. Since C eats B, they have a predator-prey (predation) relationship. Additionally, when a large number of fish C are introduced, they will consume most of the zooplankton B, leading to the near-extinction of B. With B gone, the algae A will no longer be consumed and will grow unchecked, eventually depleting resources. C will also run out of food (B) and die out, leaving only A (algae) to remain. This means C and B coexist only briefly — C cannot survive long-term without B as a food source, and B cannot survive the heavy predation pressure from C. Therefore, the relationship between C and B is both predation and competition (for resources, since both ultimately depend on the same base of algae-derived energy, and their populations are tightly linked in a way that intense predation leads to mutual elimination). Final answer: Predation and competition (predation and competition)

question: Muscle will contract when stimulated, and the changes in electric potential inside and outside the muscle cell membrane before and after the muscle is stimulated are the same as the potential changes in nerve fibers. Now take two fresh nerve-muscle specimens, and place the nerve of the left specimen on the muscle of the right specimen; at this time the nerve fiber is connected with the muscle cell (during the experiment the specimens are moistened with physiological saline), as shown in the figure. In the figure, ② and ④ refer to the junctions between nerve fibers and muscle cells; these junctions are similar to synaptic structures. Stimulating ① can cause the right muscle to contract, and the left muscle also contracts along with it. Which muscles will contract if ③ is directly stimulated?
model_answer: Both the right muscle and the left muscle will contract
cot_raw: The image shows two nerve-muscle specimens arranged side by side. The right specimen has its muscle (right muscle) and a nerve with point ① on the nerve and point ② at the junction between the nerve and the right muscle. The left specimen's nerve is placed on the right muscle, with point ③ on the left nerve and point ④ at the junction between the left nerve and the right muscle. The left muscle (left muscle) is attached to the other end of the left nerve. Stimulation point S is on the right nerve. Stimulating ① causes the right muscle to contract (nerve impulse travels from ① through the nerve to ②, then to the right muscle), and the left muscle also contracts because the impulse continues through the right muscle to ④ (nerve-muscle junction equivalent to synapse), crosses to the left nerve, travels to the left muscle, and causes it to contract. If ③ is directly stimulated on the left nerve, the impulse travels in both directions: one direction goes to ④ and then to the right muscle (since ④ is a synapse-like junction allowing transmission from nerve to muscle), causing the right muscle to contract; the other direction travels along the left nerve to the left muscle, but this is blocked at the neuromuscular junction (synapse direction is one-way — from nerve to muscle only), so the impulse cannot cross from the left nerve into the right muscle via this path, and the left muscle is not stimulated through its own nerve-muscle junction since the impulse is traveling away from it on the nerve fiber (and even if it reached the left muscle's junction, the impulse originated in the nerve and needs the nerve-muscle junction to stimulate the muscle, but the left muscle's nerve ending is not at ③'s stimulation point). Actually, stimulating ③ on the left nerve sends impulses bidirectionally along the left nerve: one direction reaches ④ and transmits to the right muscle (causing right muscle contraction), while the other direction travels to the left muscle's neuromuscular junction and causes the left muscle to contract as well. Final answer: Both the right muscle and the left muscle will contract.

question: Budding yeast belongs to unicellular eukaryotes. To search for genes related to the regulation of protein secretion, scientists used acid phosphatase (P enzyme) as an indicator to screen yeast protein secretion mutants and studied them. Chemical mutagens were used for treatment, and a mutant strain with abnormal protein secretion (sec1) was screened from yeast. Phosphate-free culture medium can promote the secretion of yeast P enzyme, and the activity of P enzyme secreted extracellularly can reflect the amount of P enzyme. Yeast was placed in phosphate-free culture medium, and the extracellular P enzyme detection results for sec1 and the wild type are shown in the figure below. According to the figure, at 24℃, the extracellular P enzyme of sec1 and the wild type increases with time. After transfer to 37℃, what trend does the extracellular P enzyme of sec1 show?
model_answer: After transfer to 37°C, the extracellular P enzyme activity of sec1 first slightly increases briefly, then continuously decreases
cot_raw: The image shows a graph plotting extracellular P enzyme activity (U·mg⁻¹, per milligram of protein) over time (hours) for two yeast strains: the wild type and the sec1 mutant (sec1). The experimental conditions are: ① cultured at 24°C (from 0–2 h), ② transferred to 37°C (from 2–4.5 h), and ③ transferred back to 24°C with a protein synthesis inhibitor added (from 4.5–7 h). For the sec1 mutant, during phase ① at 24°C, extracellular P enzyme activity rises from about 10 to 20 U·mg⁻¹. After transfer to 37°C in phase ②, the activity first slightly increases to about 20 U·mg⁻¹ around 2.5 h, then steadily decreases to a minimum of about 10 U·mg⁻¹ by 4.5 h. In phase ③, after returning to 24°C with a protein synthesis inhibitor, the activity rises again to about 27 U·mg⁻¹. In contrast, the wild type shows continuous increase throughout. Since the protein synthesis inhibitor blocks new P enzyme production in phase ③, the continued increase of sec1's extracellular P enzyme indicates that the previously accumulated (stored) P enzyme within the cell is being secreted at the permissive temperature of 24°C, meaning the sec1 mutation at 37°C caused the intracellular P enzyme to not be secreted but to accumulate inside the cell. This demonstrates that the SEC1 gene product functions in protein secretion, and at the non-permissive temperature (37°C) the sec1 mutant cannot transport P enzyme out of the cell, so extracellular P enzyme activity decreases. Final answer: After transfer to 37°C, the extracellular P enzyme activity of sec1 first slightly increases briefly, then continuously decreases.

question: Suppose a certain livestock population grazed freely on a grassland shows S-shaped growth, and the trend of the population's growth rate with changes in population size is shown in the figure. If one wants to continuously harvest as much of this livestock as possible, one should begin capturing when the population size is appropriate. Among the following four population sizes, which is appropriate?
model_answer: 丁
cot_raw: The graph shows population growth rate on the y-axis and population number on the x-axis, forming an S-shaped (sigmoid) relationship where the rate rises to a peak then falls as population increases. Four points are marked: label A and label B lie on the rising (left) side of the curve below the maximum growth rate, while label C is at the peak of the growth rate, and label D is on the descending (right) side of the curve. For an S-shaped growth curve, the population at the peak growth rate (label C) corresponds to K/2, which is the inflection point of the S-curve. To sustainably harvest the maximum amount of a population, harvesting should begin when the population is larger than K/2 so that after removal, the remaining population is at K/2 where the growth rate is highest, allowing the population to recover most rapidly. Therefore, among the four points, label D, which is located on the descending side past the peak growth rate (population greater than K/2), is the appropriate point to begin harvesting, because harvesting at this point would reduce the population to near K/2 where the maximum sustainable yield can be obtained. Final answer: D

question: The figure is a schematic diagram showing photosynthesis and respiration in a mesophyll cell of a certain plant. Answer the question: What are the substances represented by ①, ②, ③, and ④ in sequence?
model_answer: ①O₂, ②NADPH, ③ATP, ④葡萄糖 (glucose)
cot_raw: Based on the diagram, region A represents the light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis on the thylakoid membrane, where light energy, H₂O, ADP, Pi, and NADP⁺ are inputs. Region B represents the Calvin cycle (light-independent reactions) in the stroma, where CO₂ is fixed using the ATP and NADPH produced. Regions C and D represent cellular respiration processes (C is glycolysis producing pyruvate, and D includes the citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation, with acetyl-CoA, [H], and the final products CO₂ and H₂O). The numbered arrows show: ① enters the thylakoid reactions from outside, ② exits to the Calvin cycle, ③ returns from the Calvin cycle, and ④ connects the Calvin cycle to the respiration pathway. According to the photosynthetic light reactions: water is split to produce O₂, [H] (NADPH), and ATP. Therefore ① is O₂ (released when H₂O is split). ② and ③ are the products leaving the thylakoid system that drive the Calvin cycle: ② is NADPH and ③ is ATP. ④ represents the (CH₂O) / glucose produced by the Calvin cycle that enters respiration; since ④ is the arrow going from the (CH₂O) product into the glycolysis step (C) that produces pyruvate, ④ is glucose. Final answer: ①O₂, ②NADPH, ③ATP, ④glucose

question: A kind of waterbird has now been found to mainly inhabit the shallow water and mudflats of a certain lake area, and to take certain plants in the lake area as its main food source. Answer the following questions. The biological components such as the plants, waterbirds, and bacteria of the lake area and the inorganic environment constitute an ecosystem. The schematic diagram of energy flowing through this kind of waterbird on the food chain is as follows. ①, ②, and ③ indicate biological life activity processes. What are ①, ②, and ③ respectively?
model_answer: ① is the assimilation (同化) process, ② is the respiration (呼吸) process, and ③ is the decomposition (分解) process by decomposers
cot_raw: The diagram shows energy flow through a waterbird: plants are ingested by the waterbird, the energy enters process ①, from which energy is lost as heat (lost via ②), and the remaining energy is used for growth, development, and reproduction. After the waterbird dies, its remains/corpses and feces are passed to process ③. ① represents the assimilation process where the waterbird absorbs and converts ingested food energy into its own body substances. ② represents cellular respiration (or metabolism), through which part of the assimilated energy is released as heat and lost. ③ represents the decomposition process carried out by decomposers (such as bacteria), which break down the dead remains and feces to release the remaining energy. question: Researchers used instruments to detect the changes in CO2 absorption by Arabidopsis leaves under light-dark transition conditions, recording one experimental data point every 2s and presenting it as points in the figure. question: Mitochondria may have originated from symbiosis between ancient anaerobic eukaryotic cells and early bacteria. question: A student designed an experiment to study the behavior of earthworms: she prepared a large 1-square-meter tray filled with soil and divided it into four quadrants, with different conditions set in each quadrant. She placed 20 earthworms in the tray, initially 5 in each quadrant. After 20 minutes, it was found that all 20 earthworms had gathered in the high-temperature, low-humidity quadrant. What kind of behavior of earthworms did this experiment show?
model_answer: The earthworms' movement toward the high-temperature, high-salinity (hot, dry) quadrant demonstrates taxis (a directional response to environmental stimuli), showing that earthworm behavior is regulated by their nervous system in response to environmental conditions
cot_raw: The image shows a 2×2 grid of four quadrants labeled with different combinations of salinity and temperature: top-left "Low salinity, high temperature," top-right "Low salinity, low temperature," bottom-left "High salinity, high temperature," and bottom-right "High salinity, low temperature." For an experiment testing earthworm response to humidity (humidity is related to salinity/moisture in soil, since low salinity corresponds to moist soil and high salinity corresponds to dry soil), the setup implies: high temperature + low salinity (humidity) = hot, moist; high temperature + high salinity = hot, dry; low temperature + low salinity = cool, moist; low temperature + high salinity = cool, dry. The observation that all 20 earthworms moved to the high-temperature, high-salinity quadrant indicates they preferred the hot, dry conditions. The relevant biological knowledge is that earthworms have a moist, permeable skin used for cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through the skin), which must stay moist for oxygen to dissolve and diffuse in. In high-temperature environments, the skin dries out quickly, so earthworms instinctively move to environments that help them retain or restore skin moisture — but the results show they moved to the dry, hot area. The behavior of earthworms responding to environmental stimuli (temperature, humidity) through movement or posture changes, directed by the nervous system and hormones, is called taxis (specifically, kinesis or taxis). question: According to the experimental phenomena shown in the following figure, determine the substance represented by each letter E. $\\boxed{\\text{Experimental phenomena:}}$ $\\begin{array}{c} \\textbf{Experiment 1:} & \\text{Place E in a test tube, E is insoluble in water.}\\\\ \\textbf{Experiment 2:} & \\text{Place E in alcohol, E dissolves.}\\\\ \\textbf{Experiment 3:} & \\text{Place E in hydrochloric acid, E does not dissolve and no gas is produced.}\\\\ \\textbf{Experiment 4:} & \\text{Place E in sodium hydroxide solution, E does not dissolve and no gas is produced.} \\end{array}$
model_answer: [FeF₆]³⁻
cot_raw: The flowchart shows a pale green solid crystal (pale green crystal) that, when dissolved in dilute H₂SO₄, forms solution (A). Adding K₂Cr₂O₇ to (A) gives a green solution, which upon adding excess NaOH produces a colorless solution (B) and a red-brown precipitate (C). The red-brown precipitate (C) dissolves in HCl, then KSCN is added to form a blood-red solution (D). Adding NaF to (D) produces a colorless solution (E). The pale green crystal that dissolves in dilute H₂SO₄ to form solution (A) and gives a red-brown precipitate (C) with NaOH, plus a blood-red color (D) with KSCN, indicates Fe²⁺ in solution (A), so the original pale green crystal is FeSO₄·7H₂O. Solution (A) is FeSO₄, which is oxidized by K₂Cr₂O₇ to Fe₂(SO₄)₃ (green solution). Adding excess NaOH yields NaAlO₂ as the colorless solution (B) if Al³⁺ were present, but here the red-brown precipitate (C) is Fe(OH)₃, formed from Fe³⁺. The red-brown precipitate (C) dissolved in HCl gives FeCl₃, which reacts with KSCN to form the blood-red Fe(SCN)₃ solution (D). Adding NaF to Fe(SCN)₃ solution converts it to colorless [FeF₆]³⁻ complex, so the colorless solution (E) contains [FeF₆]³⁻ and Na⁺, with the iron species being [FeF₆]³⁻ (hexafluoroferrate(III) ion). The experimental phenomena given for E—insoluble in water, soluble in alcohol, insoluble in HCl without gas, and insoluble in NaOH without gas—do not match [FeF₆]³⁻ which is ionic and soluble in water; however, the flowchart evidence strongly identifies E as the [FeF₆]³⁻ complex ion in solution from the reaction Fe(SCN)₃ + 6NaF → Na₃[FeF₆] + 3NaSCN. question: The parameters of a certain atmospheric-pressure operating dryer are as follows: air conditions $t_0=20^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $H_0=0.01\,\mathrm{kg/kg}$ dry air, $t_1=120^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $t_2=70^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $H_2=0.05\,\mathrm{kg/kg}$ dry air; material conditions $\theta_1=30^\circ\mathrm{C}$, moisture content $w_1=20\%$, $\theta_2=50^\circ\mathrm{C}$, $w_2=5\%$, absolute dry material specific heat capacity $C_\mathrm{ps}=1.5\,\mathrm{kJ/(kg\cdot^\circ C)}$; the production capacity of the dryer is $53.5\,\mathrm{kg/h}$ (calculated by the product leaving the dryer), the heat loss of the dryer is neglected, what is the heat that should be supplied to the dryer? ($\mathrm{kJ/h}$)
model_answer: Q_R ≈ 1.54 × 10⁴ kJ/h (approximately 15410 kJ/h)
cot_raw: Based on the image, air enters the preheater at conditions V₁, t₀=20°C, H₀=0.01 kg/kg dry air, is heated to t₁=120°C, then enters the dryer where it picks up moisture from the wet material (w₁, θ₁) and leaves at t₂=70°C, H₂=0.05 kg/kg dry air. The dried product exits at conditions G₂, w₂, θ₂. The dryer receives heat Q_R supplied externally. Step 1: Calculate moisture evaporated per hour. Product leaving: G₂ = 53.5 kg/h with w₂ = 5%, so absolute dry material = G₂(1 − w₂) = 53.5 × 0.95 = 50.825 kg/h. Moisture in product: G₂·w₂ = 53.5 × 0.05 = 2.675 kg/h. Using dry material balance, moisture in feed: w₁/(1−w₁) = 0.20/0.80 = 0.25, so moisture entering = 50.825 × 0.25 = 12.706 kg/h. Water evaporated (mass of dry air basis, using H₂ − H₀): Actually, total water evaporated W = 12.706 − 2.675 = 10.031 kg/h. Step 2: Apply the dryer heat balance. Q_R + L·(I₁ − I₀) = L·(I₂ − I₀) + Gc·(θ₂ − θ₁) + W·θ₂ where L = mass of dry air, I = enthalpy of moist air per kg dry air, Gc = dry material rate. Enthalpy of moist air (using I = (1.01 + 1.88H)·t + 2490·H): I₀ = (1.01 + 1.88×0.01)×20 + 2490×0.01 = 20.4 + 24.9 = 45.3 kJ/kg dry air I₁ = (1.01 + 1.88×0.01)×120 + 2490×0.01 = 122.4 + 24.9 = 147.3 kJ/kg dry air I₂ = (1.01 + 1.88×0.05)×70 + 2490×0.05 = (1.104×70) + 124.5 = 77.28 + 124.5 = 201.78 kJ/kg dry air Step 3: Calculate dry air consumption. From moisture balance: L(H₂ − H₀) = W, so L = 10.031/(0.05 − 0.01) = 250.78 kg dry air/h. Step 4: Calculate heat supplied Q_R. Heat to raise air from 0°C to t₁ in preheater is provided by preheater (separate); Q_R is the heat supplied to the dryer only. Heat to heat dry material: Gc·Cp_s·(θ₂ − θ₁) = 50.825 × 1.5 × (50 − 30) = 50.825 × 30 = 1524.75 kJ/h. Heat to evaporate the remaining water in product (assumed at θ₂): the term W in the balance represents evaporation, but here W already accounts for net water removed. The heat balance (per Chinese textbook convention): Q_R = L(I₂ − I₁) + Gc·Cp_s·(θ₂ − θ₁) + (G₂·w₂)·c_w·(θ₂ − θ₁) where c_w = 4.187 kJ/(kg·°C): Q_R = 250.78 × (201.78 − 147.3) + 50.825 × 1.5 × 20 + 2.675 × 4.187 × 20 Q_R = 250.78 × 54.48 + 1524.75 + 224.0 Q_R = 13662.5 + 1524.75 + 224.0 ≈ 15411 kJ/h Final answer: Q_R ≈ 1.54 × 10⁴ kJ/h (approximately 15410 kJ/h)

question: Distribution density refers to the proportion of the distribution area of a certain geographical thing within a certain region to the total area of that region. Figure 1 is an isoline map of crop distribution density in a certain region. <image1> According to Figure 1, what is the most important factor causing the differences in the distribution of this crop?

cot_raw: Looking at Figure 1, I can observe an isoline map showing crop distribution density across a coastal region spanning approximately 31°N to 33°N latitude, with the ocean labeled in the upper right corner. The isoline values range from 0.1 in the south to 0.5 in the north, with density increasing progressively from south to north toward the coast. The isolines run roughly north-south parallel to the coastline, indicating that crop distribution density changes primarily along the latitudinal (north-south) gradient rather than along the coast-perpendicular direction. Since the entire mapped area lies within a narrow latitudinal band near 30°N along a coastline, the climatic conditions (temperature, precipitation) across this small region would be relatively similar, meaning large-scale climatic zonation cannot explain the dramatic density differences. However, the strong correlation between increasing distribution density and proximity to the ocean/coastline suggests that the closer a location is to the sea, the higher the crop distribution density becomes. The crop likely requires specific maritime conditions such as moderate temperatures, adequate moisture, and tolerance to saline coastal soils, and these conditions improve progressively as one moves northward along the coast where the growing environment becomes more favorable. Therefore, the most important factor causing the differences in crop distribution in this region is the distance from the ocean (coastline), as it directly controls the local maritime climate, soil salinity, and moisture conditions that determine whether the crop can thrive. Final answer: The distance from the ocean (proximity to the coastline), which influences the local maritime climate, moisture conditions, and soil environment suitable for the crop's growth.

question: Nobel Prize in Economics winner Arthur Lewis proposed the “dual economy” development model. Economic development is divided into two stages: first, the stage of unlimited labor supply; second, the stage of labor shortage. The intersection connecting the two stages is called the “Lewis turning point.” After the Spring Festival, the phenomenon of “difficulty recruiting workers” appeared in coastal areas and even in major labor-exporting provinces such as Jiangxi and Sichuan. The “Lewis turning point” of China’s economy may have arrived ahead of schedule. <image1> Based on this, what industrial sector is greatly affected by the appearance of the “Lewis turning point”?
model_answer: 劳动密集型产业（labor-intensive industries）
cot_raw: The image shows a diagram titled "Schematic Diagram of the Lewis Turning Point" with the vertical axis labeled P (wage level) and the horizontal axis labeled Q (quantity of labor). It depicts three downward-sloping aggregate demand curves shifting rightward: AD1 → AD2 → AD3, together with an upward-sloping total supply curve AS. The "unlimited labor supply stage" is shown on the left side, and the "labor shortage stage" on the right side, with the intersection point labeled "Lewis turning point" marked by a black dot. This illustrates that before the turning point, an abundant surplus labor force from the traditional agricultural sector flows into the modern industrial sector at a relatively constant low wage, supporting industrialization. After the turning point, surplus labor is exhausted, wages begin to rise, and the cost advantage of labor-intensive industries is lost. The question asks which industrial sector is greatly affected by the arrival of the Lewis turning point. Based on the model, the sector most dependent on cheap, abundant labor — namely labor-intensive industries (labor-intensive manufacturing such as textiles, garments, toys, footwear, and low-end electronics assembly) — will be most affected, because rising wages and labor shortages will increase production costs and erode their competitive advantage. Final answer: labor-intensive industries

question: The phenomenon in which rainfall is intercepted by plant stems and leaves is called plant interception. Its main influencing factors are plant density, plant type, season, and rainfall characteristics. The curves show that as rainfall amount increases, the maximum interception amount also increases, but at a decreasing rate, eventually approaching an upper limit. This means the larger the rainfall, the greater the absolute amount intercepted by vegetation, but the proportion of interception relative to total rainfall decreases. For soil and water conservation benefits to be the greatest, the vegetation needs to intercept a large proportion of rainfall so that less rain directly hits the soil surface, reducing surface runoff and soil erosion. The graph shows that for small rainfall amounts, the interception ratio is highest, but the absolute interception is small. However, because the 25-hour curve shows greater interception relative to rainfall amount, shorter-duration intense rainfall is intercepted effectively by dense forest vegetation. - In regions with **gently sloping terrain**, runoff is slower, allowing more time for infiltration. - The best combination for soil and water conservation is therefore in a **summer** (rainy season with concentrated precipitation) **hilly/mountainous region** with dense vegetation cover, where plant interception significantly reduces the erosive force of rainfall on the soil. Final answer: Summer, in hilly (mountainous) regions with dense vegetation, where plant interception of rainfall effectively reduces surface runoff and soil erosion.

question: Read the geological section diagram of a certain place. <image1> What is the sequence of geological events that occurred here?
model_answer: Deposition of shale and limestone → folding of these sedimentary layers → granite intrusion → faulting → erosion (unconformity) → deposition of conglomerate and sandstone
cot_raw: Looking at the diagram, I can identify the following from bottom to top and by cross-cutting relationships: shale (shale) and limestone (limestone) form the oldest folded sedimentary layers; granite (granite) intrudes into these folded layers (the intrusion cuts across them, so it is younger than them); the intrusion and folded layers are then cut by a fault (fault); above the faulted/eroded surface lie the horizontal layers of conglomerate (conglomerate) at the bottom and sandstone (sandstone) at the top. question: At 8:43 on June 14, 2008, Tokyo time, a magnitude 7.2 earthquake on the Richter scale occurred in northeastern Japan, with the focus located 15 km underground. The Japan Meteorological Agency used the “Earthquake Early Warning” system in some areas this time, gaining several seconds of varying length for residents in various places to take earthquake avoidance measures, thereby greatly reducing the losses brought by the earthquake disaster. The solid line in the figure is the graph of seismic wave velocity changing with depth: <image1> After the earthquake occurred, about how many seconds did the local seismic network gain for local residents to take emergency avoidance through the “Earthquake Early Warning System”?

Two types of waves are shown: the transverse wave with a velocity of about 4.2 km/s at the surface, and the longitudinal wave with a velocity of about 7.6 km/s at the surface. The focus is located at a depth of 15 km. The "Earthquake Early Warning System" works because the longitudinal (P) wave travels faster than the transverse (S) wave. The longitudinal wave arrives first and triggers the warning before the more destructive transverse wave arrives. For the local seismic network (located at the epicenter/surface above the focus): - The distance from the focus to the surface = 15 km - The longitudinal wave travels from the focus to the surface at about 7.6 km/s - The transverse wave travels from the focus to the surface at about 4.2 km/s Time for the longitudinal wave to reach the surface: t₁ = 15 km ÷ 7.6 km/s ≈ 1.97 s Time for the transverse wave to reach the surface: t₂ = 15 km ÷ 4.2 km/s ≈ 3.57 s The warning time gained is the time difference between the arrival of the longitudinal wave and the transverse wave: Δt = t₂ - t₁ = 3.57 s - 1.97 s ≈ 1.6 s Final answer: approximately 1.6 seconds

question: Abu Simbel Temple is located 280 kilometers south of the Aswan Dam. It was built in 1257 BC by Ramesses II, a pharaoh of the 19th Dynasty of ancient Egypt, because of his worship of the sun god. The temple has a 61 m long tunnel, and a statue of the pharaoh stands at the end of the tunnel. Only on the early mornings of two specific days in a year can sunlight pass through the tunnel and shine on the statue of the pharaoh at the end. Read the figure and answer: <image1> If the two days when sunlight enters the end of the tunnel are regularly distributed in time within a year, and if Ramesses II's birthday is April 21, then which day is most likely the enthronement date he selected?
model_answer: March 21 (the spring equinox)
cot_raw: The image shows a horizontal cross-section of a long tunnel with a statue chamber on the left side, and an arrow labeled "sunlight" entering from the right side pointing leftward into the tunnel, indicating that sunlight must travel straight through the entire 61 m length to reach the statue at the far end. This geometry means the sun's rays must enter perpendicular to the tunnel's opening, so the sun must be positioned due east (or due west) relative to the temple for light to reach the statue at sunrise (or sunset). Since sunlight only reaches the statue at the end of the tunnel when the sun rises due east (or sets due west), this can only occur on the two days when the sun is directly over the equator—the equinoxes. This gives the vernal equinox (around March 21) and the autumnal equinox (around September 23). The two days are evenly distributed in the year, corresponding to the spring equinox (March 21) and the autumn equinox (September 23). Given that Ramesses II's birthday is April 21, the day nearest to it among the two special days is the spring equinox on March 21. Therefore, the date he most likely selected for his enthronement is the spring equinox day, March 21. Final answer: March 21 (the spring equinox)

question: The area shown in the figure below has widespread frozen soil. Frozen soil has a unique influence on the development of landforms. According to the characteristics of the area shown in the figure, what type of river valley is likely to form here? <image1>

A cold front is indicated extending southward from the low-pressure center across the region, showing cold air pushing from the northwest toward the southeast. This setup represents a high-latitude area in Northeast Asia (such as Northeast China or adjacent parts of Russia) where winters are extremely cold, permafrost (frozen soil) develops widely, and surface water often freezes. In such cold regions with widespread permafrost, the ground remains frozen for much of the year, but the active layer near the surface thaws during the short summer. Because the underlying permafrost is impermeable, meltwater and rainwater cannot infiltrate deeply, so they flow along the surface. Frost heaving caused by repeated freeze–thaw cycles also fractures and loosens surface materials. These conditions cause river valleys to widen and their floors to become broad and flat, while vertical (downward) erosion is limited because the frozen subsoil resists deep cutting. As a result, the typical valley shape developed in permafrost regions is a broad, U-shaped valley with a wide, flat floor — often described as a "U-shaped valley" (trough-shaped broad valley) characteristic of periglacial, permafrost environments. Final answer: A broad, U-shaped valley with a wide, flat floor (typical of permafrost/frozen-soil regions).

question: Peat, also called grass peat or peat coal, is a substance accumulated over a long period from incompletely decomposed organic remains (mainly plant remains). It mainly forms in swamp areas. The development of peat depends on the growth amount of swamp plants and the decomposition amount of remains. Peat that is still accumulating in modern swamp lands is called exposed peat. Read the distribution of exposed peat in China (Figure 1) and the changes over time in decomposition rates of different types of plants at a certain place (Figure 2). <image1> Peat has many uses and can produce huge economic benefits. The decomposition rate graph over a year shows four different plants with varying decomposition rates. To maximize peat accumulation for economic benefit, the goal is to find the plant that produces the most net organic matter, meaning its growth amount minus its decomposition amount should be the greatest. The graph indicates that deciduous leaves and moss have the lowest decomposition rates throughout the year, which means more of their dead organic matter remains incompletely decomposed and can accumulate to form peat. In contrast, grass and herbaceous flowers have much higher decomposition rates, causing most of their remains to decompose and release back into the environment rather than forming peat. Since the decomposition rate is a key limiting factor in peat formation, selecting a plant with a low decomposition rate ensures higher net accumulation of organic remains, which leads to faster peat formation and greater economic returns from peat production. Among the two, moss is typically the dominant peat-forming plant in the cold, waterlogged swamp environments of China's major peat regions (Northeast and Qinghai-Tibet), as it thrives in acidic, anaerobic conditions that further inhibit decomposition and promote peat accumulation. question: Read the topographic profile along 106.8°E and the curve chart of annual average precipitation at places along the profile, and answer the question. <image1> The nighttime rainfall amount in terrain region 4 accounts for 60%~70% of the total precipitation. From the perspective of atmospheric radiation conditions, what is the main characteristic at night?
model_answer: At night, the sky in region 4 is often cloudy with thick cloud cover, which strongly absorbs ground longwave radiation and returns it to the surface (strong atmospheric counter-radiation / weak effective radiation), so the ground cools slowly; the warm, moist air near the surface rises gradually along the mountain slopes, producing sustained nighttime precipitation

At night in terrain region 4, which consists of extensive mountainous areas, clouds frequently form and persist. These clouds have a strong effect on atmospheric radiation: they strongly absorb the longwave radiation emitted from the Earth's surface (ground radiation) and then radiate this energy back downward (counter-radiation/atmospheric counter-radiation). question: In the process in which tectonic movement forms river terraces, during the stable period of tectonic movement, what processes are rivers mainly dominated by?

question: Due to an increase in the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere, how will the range of mid-latitude inland grasslands change?
model_answer: The range of mid-latitude inland grasslands will shift poleward (northward in the Northern Hemisphere) and overall shrink in area, because rising temperatures from increased greenhouse gases push the subtropical high-pressure belt and its associated arid conditions poleward, making interior continental regions drier
cot_raw: Based on the map, the area shown is the Arabian Peninsula and surrounding regions, with the location Doha marked at approximately 25°N, situated between the Tropic of Cancer (20°N shown) and 40°N latitude. The map depicts a mid-latitude inland region in the Northern Hemisphere. The key geographic principle here relates to how climate zones shift with changes in global temperature. Mid-latitude inland grasslands exist in semi-arid conditions with moderate temperatures and limited but sufficient precipitation. Their northern and southern boundaries are determined by climatic factors including temperature and moisture availability. The formula/principle relevant here is that a doubling of atmospheric CO₂ is expected to raise global mean temperatures by approximately 2–4°C, and each 1°C of warming shifts climate zones poleward by roughly 100–150 km in mid-latitudes. This occurs because increased greenhouse gases trap more outgoing longwave radiation, warming the lower atmosphere and pushing the subtropical high-pressure belts (around 30°N) and associated arid conditions poleward. Because the subtropical high-pressure belt is the primary controller of aridity at these latitudes (it produces descending air that suppresses precipitation), its poleward shift would bring drier conditions to existing grassland regions. Simultaneously, the northern boundary of these grasslands would shift into what are currently cooler, moister zones, but the overall trend in interior continental areas at mid-latitudes in the Northern Hemisphere is toward drying as the dry subtropical climate expands poleward. Final answer: The range of mid-latitude inland grasslands will shift poleward (northward in the Northern Hemisphere) and overall shrink in area, because rising temperatures from increased greenhouse gases push the subtropical high-pressure belt and its associated arid conditions poleward, making interior continental regions drier.

question: A truck and a passenger car are traveling in the same lane on a highway, with the passenger car in front and the truck behind. An emergency situation suddenly occurs, and the two vehicles brake at the same time. At the beginning of braking, the two vehicles are 30m apart. During braking, the v-t graph of the two vehicles is as shown in the figure. Judge according to the graph: will the two vehicles have a rear-end collision? If so, does the rear-end collision occur before or after the passenger car stops?
model_answer: Yes, a rear-end collision occurs, and it happens at the moment the passenger car stops (at t = 10 s)

The truck starts at v₀₂ = 40 m/s and decelerates to 0 at t = 30 s, giving a deceleration of a₂ = 4/3 m/s². Both lines intersect at t = 10 s at v = 0, meaning the passenger car stops while the truck is still moving. To check for a collision, compare the distances traveled by each vehicle. The passenger car travels x₁ = ½ × 30 × 10 = 150 m. The truck travels x₂ = ½ × 40 × 30 = 600 m in 30 s, but we need to compare distances starting from the truck's position. Let d₁ be the truck's distance traveled in 10 s: d₁ = ½ × 40 × 10 + ½ × 10 × (40 − 40/3) = 200 + 200/3 ≈ 266.7 m, and using the truck's equation of motion d₁ = 40(10) − ½(4/3)(10)² = 400 − 200/3 ≈ 333.3 m. The distance the truck travels exceeds that of the passenger car by 333.3 − 150 = 183.3 m, which is greater than the 30 m initial gap, so a rear-end collision definitely occurs. Therefore the gap reaches its minimum precisely when the passenger car stops, so the collision occurs exactly as the passenger car comes to a stop. question: As shown in the figure, a closed conducting ring is fixed horizontally. A bar magnet with its S pole downward, with initial velocity v0, falls along the vertical axis passing through the center of the conducting ring. During the process of passing through the conducting ring, viewed from top to bottom, how does the direction of the induced current in the conducting ring change successively?
model_answer: Clockwise, then counterclockwise (顺时针，再逆时针)
cot_raw: The image shows a horizontal closed conducting ring with a bar magnet falling vertically along the central axis above it, moving downward with initial velocity v₀. The S pole of the magnet faces downward (toward the ring), so as the magnet approaches, magnetic field lines point upward through the ring (entering the S pole from above means field lines go into S, so below S pole field lines point downward... let me reconsider: field lines exit N pole and enter S pole, so below an S-pointing-down magnet, field lines point upward into the S pole, meaning the flux through the ring points upward and increases in magnitude as the magnet approaches). Key analysis: The magnetic flux Φ through the ring (taking upward as positive) is upward and increasing as the magnet approaches (before reaching the ring center). By Lenz's law, the induced current opposes this change, so it creates a downward magnetic field inside the ring. Using the right-hand rule viewed from top to bottom, the induced current flows clockwise when viewed from above. When the magnet passes through the center of the ring, the flux is at a maximum (still upward), and the rate of change is momentarily zero, so the induced current is zero at this instant. As the magnet moves below the ring and continues downward away from it, the upward flux through the ring decreases in magnitude. The induced current now opposes this decrease by trying to maintain the upward flux, so the induced current creates an upward magnetic field inside the ring. Viewed from top to bottom, this means the induced current flows counterclockwise. Therefore, viewed from top to bottom, the induced current flows clockwise first (as the magnet approaches and passes through the ring), then counterclockwise (as the magnet moves away below the ring). Final answer: Clockwise, then counterclockwise (clockwise, then counterclockwise)
